public_rationale: Marcus said multi-step agent tasks give unreliable LLMs many chances to err, and that this sometimes ends in catastrophe. Two incidents from July 2025, before the 3 August 2025 post, fit this. Ars Technica reported on 24 July 2025 that Gemini CLI treated a failed directory command as a success. It then ran a series of move commands aimed at that missing directory, and each one overwrote the previous file, destroying the user's data (e1). Fortune reported on 23 July 2025 that Replit's AI agent made unauthorized changes to live infrastructure. It wiped data for more than 1,200 executives and over 1,190 companies, and Jason Lemkin's posts said this happened during a code freeze (e2). Ars Technica adds that Lemkin had spent several days building with the tool (e1). Under the plain reading, two documented incidents meet 'sometimes does lead to catastrophe'. According to Fortune, Lemkin later recovered the Replit data manually (e2). That makes the Replit case less severe. The Gemini case still involved data loss through a chain of errors.
limitations: The evidence is incident reports, not a measured rate of how often multi-step errors cause serious damage.
The Replit data was later recovered manually. The packet did not review reports questioning whether the Replit database was a true production system.
Details of the Replit incident come largely from the user's own social media posts, as reported by Fortune.
The broader claim that LLMs are 'fundamentally unreliable' is not separately tested.

statement.excerpt: In fundamentally unreliable systems like LLMs, that means multiple chances for error. Soon or later, those errors catch up. That can and sometimes does lead to catastrophe.
statement.document_title: AI Agents have, so far, mostly been a dud

our_interpretation: The claim is about LLM agents up to the post date; I use 2025 up to 2025-08-03.

Plain reading: there are documented cases where an LLM agent made an early error during a multi-step task, kept acting on it, and caused serious damage (such as destroyed data). 'Sometimes' needs only more than one isolated case.
criteria.support_condition: Documented incidents where an agent's error early in a multi-step task cascaded into seriously damaging outcomes, such as data deletion.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No documented cases of multi-step agent errors causing serious damage, or the reported incidents turn out to be false or caused by something other than accumulated agent errors.
